articles.title: AI: What is it? Can it be stopped? BBC correspondent answers
articles.summary: The BBC's AI correspondent Marc Cieslak explains what artificial intelligence is and whether it could cause a threat to humanity.
articles.body:

articles.title: The Best Retinol Body Lotions, According to Dermatologists
articles.summary: Retinol can give you firmer-looking skin and boost collagen production. Shop the best expert-recommended formulas from Paula’s Choice, Soft Services, Necessaire and more.
articles.body: Body lotions can be a means to an end: Slather it on and let your skin drink up the moisture. But the best formulas lend an extra something to your body-care routine. Enter: body lotions with retinol. The vitamin A derivative is well-loved by many dermatologists and NBC Selected editors for its ability to even out skin tone and texture. “Retinol smooths rough patches, fades discoloration, and boosts collagen production for firmer, more youthful-looking skin,” says board-certified dermatologist Dr. Helyn Alvarez. “Think of it as a skin reset button.” And while retinol creams and serums are a mainstay for many people’s facial routine, the ingredient can offer many benefits below the neck, too. “It’s especially great for areas like the chest, arms, and even knees, where fine lines and crepey skin can sneak up over time,” says Alvarez. With that in mind, I spoke with three dermatologists to compile a list of retinol body lotions worth adding to your daily regimen. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best retinol body lotions This body lotion pairs retinol with moisturizing shea butter and grapeseed oil; together, they help reduce dryness and improve the look of uneven skin texture, according to the brand. It’s ideal for those who are new to retinol, according to Alvarez, who calls it “a gentle, beginner-friendly retinol body lotion that smooths skin, evens tone, and hydrates.” It’s mild enough for daily use, too, she says. Board-certified dermatologist Dr. Arash Akhavan also recommends it, noting that it has added vitamin C to improve skin texture. Plus, he says, the 0.1% concentration of retinol makes it appropriate for patients with sensitive skin. SkinBetter’s AlphaRet technology, which pairs retinol with alpha hydroxy acids (a type of chemical exfoliant), is popular among dermatologists, who incorporate it into their own facial skin-care routines. It’s now available for the rest of the body in this formula, which helps resurface skin, according to the brand. Alvarez calls the treatment “luxurious,” saying that it’s “perfect for dry, aging or crepey skin that needs both renewal and deep moisture.” Board-certified dermatologist Dr. Carmen Castilla also says that the combination “works into the skin easily and does not leave a greasy residue.” This all-over night cream includes retinol as well as peptides — which help support collagen and elastin production — and moisturizing ingredients like shea and cocoa butters. It’s gentle enough for daily use, according to the brand, and Castilla likes that it has a lower, but still effective concentration of retinol that’s safe for sensitive skin types. For seasoned retinol users, Akhavan considers this potent formula a good way to increase efficacy, since it combines retinol with glycolic and lactic acids. While that might sound intense, the addition of hyaluronic acid adds hydration to skin, which he says can help “decrease some of the potential irritation from retinol use.” It can also help with issues like crepiness and dark spots. “With regular use, patients can expect smoother skin texture and potential improvement in signs of sun damage as well,” he says. What sets this body lotion apart is that the retinol is encapsulated, meaning that it’s stored in a capsule that’s designed to penetrate the skin with less irritation; to further buffer its effects, the formula has moisturizers like shea butter and allantoin. On top of that, experts have told us that the formula has a great texture that’s rich yet not greasy or heavy — making it one of our favorite body lotions for mature skin — and the accessible price point is also a plus. This is a body serum, so it’s more lightweight than a body lotion. “This body serum has a moisturizing milky texture, which I much prefer to the oily feel I often associate serums with,” says NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin, who was sent a sample by the brand. “When I rub it into my skin, it absorbs in seconds and doesn’t leave behind a greasy residue. I also didn’t notice much, if any, scent, which is great because I’m very scent sensitive.” It blends retinol with 5% niacinamide (an anti-inflammatory ingredient) and 3% glycerin (which hydrates). I used this body treatment after having my baby, since I had some hyperpigmentation during pregnancy. Not only is my skin smoother, but it’s also noticeably brighter — which makes sense, since it has niacinamide and vitamin C, which are two ingredients known for their ability to even skin tone. It also has hydrating ingredients like hyaluronic acid, so in the summer, it’s moisturizing enough to serve as my body lotion. “I’ve never been great about consistently using body lotion — I hate how it often leaves my skin feeling greasy,” says NBC Selected commerce editor Bethany Heitman. “But as I get older, my skin feels drier and isn’t as perky as it once was. I started using this and love how quickly it absorbs. I’ve been using it for about a month and I definitely notice my skin looks a bit more plump.” Along with retinol, the lotion contains lipids and niacinamide to help nourish the skin barrier, according to the brand. It also has a sweet vanilla scent. This lotion contains encapsulated retinol, which is thought to be more stable and less likely to degrade, according to the brand. It also has cocoa butter and squalane to help replenish the moisture our bodies naturally lose as we age. Reviewers appreciate that it is lightweight and fragrance-free. How I picked the best retinol body lotion First, I talked to three dermatologists who shared what they recommend looking for in a retinol body lotion. Because retinol comes in different strengths — and can require some getting used to — beginners and regular users might need differing concentrations. When creating this list, I considered: Retinol concentration: The higher the concentration, the more powerful the retinol. That means newbies should start with a lower concentration.Additional ingredients: Moisturizers like hyaluronic acid and shea butter can help keep skin comfortable and offset the drying effects of retinol.Fragrance: Some people, especially those with sensitive skin, may not want fragrance in their formulas, since it can be potentially irritating. How to shop for retinol body lotion The most important thing to keep in mind when shopping is the lotion’s retinol concentration, since retinol products can vary widely in strength, according to Akhavan. You can usually find them with anywhere between 0.1% and 0.5% retinol, which, he says, can “strike a good balance between efficacy and tolerability.” If you’ve never used retinol before, start with a lower number. “The skin on your body is thicker than your face, but that doesn’t mean you should go full throttle from day one,” says Alvarez. “0.1% to 0.3% is a good starting point.” Then, if your skin tolerates it well — meaning it’s not dry, itchy or otherwise irritated — then you can gradually move to a product with a higher concentration, she says. Packaging is also important. A bottle or tube that’s airtight and opaque (meaning light doesn’t get in) “is essential for retinol products, as the ingredient is highly unstable,” says Akhavan. In other words, retinol breaks down more quickly when exposed to light and air, making it less effective. Take a good look at the ingredient list. “Formulations with the same concentration can have different effects on the skin depending on the other ingredients they are paired with,” says Akhavan. For example, a 0.1% retinol body lotion that includes alpha hydroxy acids — which have an exfoliating effect — can be more effective (but also potentially more drying) than a 0.1% retinol body lotion alone. He recommends looking for retinol paired with moisturizing ingredients to make it more tolerable.Know when not to use retinol — namely, during pregnancy, says Castilla. In that case, stick with a retinol alternative. The same goes if you find that your skin is irritated or uncomfortable even with a low-concentration retinol body lotion. She focuses on both medical and cosmetic dermatology.Dr. Arash Akhaven, FAAD, is a board-certified dermatologist and founder of The Dermatology & Laser Group in New York, NY. articles.title: 11 Best Space Heaters of 2026, According to Experts | NBC Select
articles.summary: Need to buy a space heater? Here are expert tips for choosing the best space heater, including options from Dyson, Lasko, Jnrdo and other brands.
articles.body: Space heaters are a fast and affordable way to warm up your home when temperatures dip — and they can be a beneficial tool to keep on hand in case of emergencies. Whether it’s a drafty bedroom or outside on the patio during a cool night, space heaters can give an effective boost of heat wherever you need it. To determine the best one for you, I spoke to home and safety experts about the benefits of space heaters, what features to look for when shopping for one and how to use them safely. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best space heaters Listed below are expert-recommended options at various price points. Editor’s pick This space heater comes recommended by NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown, who loves how quickly it warms up. “This heater is small but it packs a punch. On the highest level, it heats up a large room in under an hour,” she says. “There’s also a mechanism on the bottom that can gauge if it’s sitting on a flat surface or not. If it’s not, it will automatically turn off, which I love.” The heater is made of comes with three temperature setting and a built-in handle so you can easily carry it from room to room. Best radiant space heater Glenn Wiseman, sales manager of Top Hat Home Comfort Services in Ontario, recommends this portable infrared model for its dual heating system and built-in thermostat that ranges from 50 to 85 degrees Fahrenheit. The energy-saving space heater offers 1,500 watts and is powered through an electric cord with 120 volts, which can evenly heat a 150-square-foot room, he says. It also has an automatic 12-hour shutoff timer. Best radiant space heater for large rooms This RealSmart infrared space heater is for spaces up to 350 square feet. It has a maximum setting of 1,500 watts, a remote and three different heat modes. It also includes an ”eco setting,” which the brand says maintains a constant 68-degree temperature using less power for when you want to bring it into a smaller room. Best panel radiant space heater The nice thing about this lightweight, compact space heater is that it can either be mounted on the wall or set on the floor. It also comes with wheels so you can easily move it from room to room. It packs a powerful punch with 1,500 watts of heat and has an adjustable thermostat and multiple heat settings so you can personalize for your comfort, according to the brand. Best wall-mounted convection space heater Arie Van Tuijl, a licensed home inspector and founder of home-maintenance website Home Inspector Secrets,recommends this wall-mounted, convection space heater, which has a temperature-controlling thermostat and the brand’s Wall-Sens technology, which cuts out the power for safety when the unit is removed from the wall, according to the brand. The unit, which Envi says heats rooms between 130 and 150 square feet, is just 2 inches thick and can automatically dim the power light in dark rooms. Best tower convection space heater This Lasko space heater has a bladeless design at a more affordable price than similar brands, like Dyson. Lasko says it’s equipped with a slew of safety features, including a safe touch surface and an automatic 8-hour shut-off switch. With its quiet oscillating mode, this tower can evenly distribute heat in rooms up to 300 square feet, according to the brand. Best combination space heater This oscillating tower unit is both a space heater and fan. It has four fan speeds and three heat settings, according to the brand. It also comes with a 6-foot power cord, a remote and has a 1 to 8-hour auto shut-off feature. Best energy-efficient combination space heater Van Tuijl recommends this convection space heater from Dreo due to its easy-to-use touch screen panel, strong heat output and remote control capabilities. This model has three heating modes and a digital thermostat that ranges from 41 degrees to 95 degrees Fahrenheit. It also has a timer that automatically shuts off after 12 hours, and the remote lets you turn the unit off from up to 26 feet away, according to the brand. Best luxury space heater The bladeless Dyson Pure Hot + Cold is a remote-controlled combination heater, fan and air purifier all in one, according to the brand. The remote-controlled fan can oscillate up to 350 degrees and offers different modes, including a backward airflow mode that diverts air through the rear of the space heater, continuing its purifying effect without the draft, according to the brand. It also includes a nighttime mode with a dimmed display, according to Dyson. Wiseman noted this space heater is “substantially quieter” than many other models and can regulate indoor air quality: using a HEPA-style filter, it can capture 99.97 percent of particles that are 0.3 microns in size, says the brand. The unit can also connect to Wi-Fi so you can control your machine remotely and schedule when your air purifier is on, using the Dyson Link app. Best budget space heater The portable Lasko Oscillating Ceramic Heater, is a worthwhile option if you’re on a budget: besides our editor's pick, it's the most affordable one on our list. Lasko says this space heater can heat rooms up to 300 square feet and offers two heat levels — low heat and high heat — along with a cool air fan setting. You can also use the thermostat knob to both turn on the unit and have it shut off automatically once a certain temperature has been reached (though the knob itself doesn’t list actual numbers), according to the brand. Best safety features This compact and portable heater from DeLonghi packs 1,500 watts of power and is great for all-season use; it has heat settings for the winter and a cooling, fan-only functionality that’s perfect for summertime, according to the brand. You can customize your heat settings using the adjustable thermostat and also carry the heater with you using the cool-touch handle at the top. This heater also has a number of built-in safety features that make it easier to have around a busy home, including a two-stage protection against overheating and an internal tip-over switch that automatically shuts the heater off if it falls over, according to the brand. How I picked the best space heaters There are several factors to consider when choosing a space heater. Here’s everything I kept in mind when making this list: Type: The main types of space heaters are radiant, convection and combination. Radiant heaters primarily warm what’s directly in front of them with infrared heat rather than your entire home or room. A convection heater is more suited to heating a room or large space. A combination heater has a fan that propels hot air outward to heat a home — they’re louder than radiant and convection ones, but less of a fire hazard, according to our experts. All three types of space heaters are included in the list above.Testing: Like with many home appliances, space heaters are tested by independent quality assurance agencies, mainly the Underwriters Laboratories (UL) or the Electrical Testing Laboratories (ETL), to ensure they meet the agency’s safety requirements. Most of the space units above have either UL or ETL certification.Wattage: The power of a space heater is measured in watts. The higher the wattage, the more powerful it is and the larger of a space it can heat, according to Van Tuijl. Tuijl generally recommends buying a space heater that is in the 500-1,000 watts range for smaller rooms (which are typically considered 120 square feet or less), and between 1,000 and 1,500 watts for larger rooms. The list above includes space heaters with wattage ranging between 500 and 1,500.Safety features: Space heaters can be potential fire hazards, so it’s important that they include safety features like protective grills and an auto shut-off feature. Many of the space heaters listed above have an auto shut-off feature, tip-over safety feature or protective grill. Warranty. Most space heaters come with a warranty so you can be sure that the product is returnable or replaceable if something happens to it, according to Glenn Wiseman, sales manager of Top Hat Home Comfort Services in Ontario. I included all of the warranties for the units above, where possible. How to shop for a space heater Once you’ve decided that you want a space heater, factor in the aspects below to choose the exact one that’s best for your space and situation. Decide on a type Choose between a radiant, convection or combination space heater. Depending on your living situation, one may be better for you than the other. If you have a small space, choose a radiant heater and if you have a large space to warm up, a convection may be best. Additionally, if you don’t mind the noise, a combination space heater is good for families with small children since they’re less of a safety hazard, according to our experts. Consider where you’ll put it In addition to the type of space heater you want, you should consider where you’ll put it, which will determine what size and shape is best. Plus, if you’re only getting one to heat a small room, this will further make it easier to decide on a type. Noise level Some space heaters tend to make a lot of noise, some more than others. Keeping this in mind, I made sure to include units from brands that mention minimal to moderate noise. units are louder than others. If you’re shopping for a bedroom or home office, that’s something to keep in mind. One resource for finding devices that are especially quiet is Quiet Mark, which tests and awards products based on their noise output. Take energy efficiency into account Space heaters are generally more energy efficient than central heating since you’re only heating up the room and some space heaters are also more energy efficient than others. Since space heaters don’t have Energy Star ratings — which independently certifies a product’s energy efficiency — the easiest way to determine if your unit conserves energy is by checking whether it has features like an adjustable thermostat and auto shut-off option that can maintain a certain temperature and prevent a room from overheating, according to the Department of Energy. What should you know about space heaters and safety? The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission estimates more than 25,000 residential fires are associated with the use of space heaters every year, and an estimated 6,000 people go to the emergency room for burn injuries associated with contacting the hot surfaces of heaters. To prevent fires and injuries, many experts recommend looking for space heaters that are tested by independent safety laboratories, like Intertek (ETL) and Underwriters Laboratories (UL). Joel Hawk, principal engineering manager for small appliances at UL, tells us that these laboratories test space heaters based on nationally recognized safety standards, and add that space heaters can be very safe as long as they’re used per the instructions. While the features that can certify products as “reasonably safe” vary from one space heater to the other, Hawk says his engineers typically look at whether the product adequately responds to overheating conditions or a malfunction (and if it permanently shuts down in unsafe conditions) and whether there are features that prevent electric shock, like suitable insulation and heat-resistant cords. Another important attribute that’s tested is what Hawk calls “personal injury” — UL tests to ensure the unit won’t catch fire and that there aren’t surfaces hot enough to cause a thermal burn or moving parts that may cause injury if they’re touched. While independent testing and built-in safety features from the manufacturer can mean a space heater is functionally safe, our experts note that common sense also plays a big role in safety. The CPSC recommends the following safety tips to minimize the risk of fire: Never leave a heater operating while unattended or while you are sleeping.Keep combustible material like papers, clothes, beds and curtains at least 3 feet from the front, sides and back of the heater.Avoid powering the heater with an extension cord or power strip.Place the heater on a stable, level surface where it won’t be knocked over. To prevent electrical shocks, always keep electric heaters away from water, and never touch an electric heater if you’re wet. articles.title: Ludhiana encounter: Police shoot 2 hitmen 1km away from where they were to strike
articles.summary: Ludhiana police killed two suspected hitmen in an encounter near a memorial event; three 9mm pistols, 50 rounds seized; gang links to Davinder Bambiha.
articles.body: LUDHIANA: Police killed two suspected hitmen in an encounter Sunday afternoon, intercepting them just one km from a memorial event they were allegedly sent to attack in Ludhiana.Police commissioner Swapan Sharma said the two, identified as Karanjot Singh alias Nona and Sandeep Singh, both from Amritsar, were sent by wanted gangsters Balwinder Singh alias Dony Bal and Shaganpreet Singh, key operatives of the Davinder Bambiha gang, to open fire at a blood donation camp.The event was organised on Dugri Road in memory of former Congress village sarpanch Rajwinder Singh Grewal alias Ravi Khwajke, who was shot dead by Bambiha and his associates during a wedding function near Gill Road on Feb 20, 2016.Joint teams from the Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) and Ludhiana city police engaged the suspects who were on a motorcycle near the Atam Nagar police post after receiving an intelligence tip-off.Sharma said the suspects opened fire on police officers after being cornered, hitting a police vehicle twice during an exchange of more than 25 rounds before being shot dead in retaliatory fire.Police recovered three 9mm automatic handguns, including a Turkish-made Zigana and a Pakistani Glock, along with 50 live rounds and a motorcycle from the encounter site. Police said the weapons were smuggled across the border.Police suspect their additional accomplices on separate vehicles may have escaped.Both the shooters had criminal background. While Karanjot had been booked in Arms Act, robbery and NDPS Act cases, Sandeep faced one criminal case, according to police.AGTF deputy superintendent Rajan Parminder Singh said, “Police suspect the gunmen had a particular target to kill at the memorial. However, the kind of weapons and ammunition they were carrying, they could have caused multiple casualties.”Police investigations are ongoing.In Jan 2022, a local court convicted a Moga resident and sentenced him to rigorous life imprisonment in the 2016 Khwajke murder case. articles.summary: Candidato ao governo do Paraná foi o primeiro da série de entrevistas exibida a partir desta segunda (14) no telejornal Meio-Dia Paraná, da RPC, afiliada da TV Globo.
articles.body:
Sergio Moro ( PL ), candidato ao governo do Paraná nas eleições de 2026, afirmou que pretende criar uma "Agência Estadual de Combate à Corrupção" no Paraná, se eleito. Moro também afirmou que pretende participar do debate entre os candidatos ao governo organizado pela RPC, afiliada da TV Globo no Paraná, no dia 29 de setembro. Desde o início da campanha eleitoral, Moro não esteve em nenhum dos debates entre candidatos. Assista à íntegra da entrevista no vídeo acima.

“Vamos criar nossa Agência Estadual Anticorrupção. Aqui no Paraná nós vamos ser modelo para o restante do país. Se Brasília abandonou o combate à corrupção e hoje nos entristece, nós vamos ter nossa agência para não deixar acontecer. Porque cada centavo economizado do desvio do dinheiro público é dinheiro que a gente vai utilizar na saúde, na educação e na infraestrutura”, disse Moro.

O candidato disse que vai colocar na agência "os melhores servidores públicos”, com uma diretoria com mandato de quatro anos.

A fala foi feita em entrevista ao vivo no telejornal Meio Dia Paraná, na RPC, afiliada da TV Globo, nesta segunda-feira (14). Ao longo da semana, os candidatos Requião Filho (PDT) e Sandro Alex (PSD) também serão entrevistados. Veja abaixo as datas das entrevistas.

Sobre a participação no debate eleitoral organizado pela emissora, Moro disse que vai participar e afirmou que não tem “nenhum problema com debate qualificado” e que os anteriores estavam ainda "prematuros".

Sérgio Moro, candidato ao Governo do Paraná — Foto: Manuella Mariani/g1

Entrevistas com os candidatos ao governo do Paraná na RPC

A entrevista com Sergio Moro foi a primeira da série de entrevistas exibidas ao vivo pela RPC no telejornal Meio-Dia Paraná. Serão ouvidos os três candidatos que aparecem melhor colocados no cenário estimulado da última pesquisa Quaest de intenção de voto para o governo do estado.

Além de Moro, serão ouvidos os candidatos Sandro Alex (PSD), na terça-feira (15), e Requião Filho (PDT), na quarta-feira (16). A ordem das entrevistas foi definida por meio de sorteio, realizado na presença de representantes dos partidos:

Sergio Moro (PL) - entrevista na segunda-feira (14)

Sandro Alex (PSD) - entrevista na terça-feira (15)

Requião Filho (PDT) - entrevista na quarta-feira (16)

O tempo das entrevistas é de 30 minutos, com mais um minuto para considerações finais, para cada candidato.

Os demais candidatos ao governo do Paraná terão entrevistas gravadas de um minuto, exibidas também no Meio Dia Paraná, na sexta-feira (18).

Na entrevista desta segunda-feira, Sergio Moro foi perguntado sobre os seguintes temas:

Código de ética para o alto escalão do governo;

Gastos com deslocamentos durante mandato como senador;

Aliança com o candidato Flávio Bolsonaro;

Código de ética para o alto escalão do governo

A entrevista começou com uma pergunta sobre a proposta de criação de um código de ética para o alto escalão do governo, prevista no plano de governo do candidato. Quando atuava como juiz, Moro tinha um salário de quase R$ 30 mil e também recebia um auxílio-moradia, mesmo sendo proprietário de um apartamento em Curitiba, onde trabalhava. À época, Moro justificou que o benefício servia para compensar a falta de reajuste salarial dos juízes. Questionado se usar o auxílio como aumento salarial seria ético e moral, o candidato disse que "ninguém combateu mais a corrupção".

Afirmou ainda que sua intenção, caso eleito, é criar uma “Agência Estadual de Combate à Corrupção”, que deverá ser administrada por funcionários públicos para fiscalizar possíveis fraudes em licitações e enriquecimentos ilícitos. Afirmou ainda que a diretoria deste órgão terá um mandato de quatro anos, para que não sofra “pressões políticas”.

Sobre os “penduricalhos” – valores incluídos nos salários – dos juízes, o candidato atribuiu os valores do auxílio-moradia a um "descontrole" de Brasília, mas que é preciso tratar deste assunto com transparência.

Gastos com deslocamentos durante mandato como senador

Ao ser questionado sobre os gastos de R$ 720 mil em seu mandato como senador, sendo o oitavo senador com mais gastos desse tipo no país, Sergio Moro afirmou que, ao ser eleito em 2022, se comprometeu em ser um “senador itinerante”, para estar perto da população e ouvir suas necessidades. Disse ainda que não enriqueceu com este dinheiro. Segundo ele, as viagens e gastos foram para conhecer as realidades das pessoas e que vai continuar viajando.

Durante este tópico, Moro disse que vai cortar os gastos com regulações, cargos e burocracias desnecessários para um “choque de gestão” no Governo do Estado.

Sobre ter sido obrigado pela Justiça Eleitoral a retirar do ar a propaganda eleitoral em que afirmava que o governador Ratinho Junior era seu aliado em 2018 (quando Moro ainda era juiz federal) e em 2022 (quando Ratinho Junior declarou apoio público ao então candidato ao Senado Paulo Martins), Sergio Moro negou ter tentado "pegar carona" na popularidade do atual governador. Disse que respeita a decisão judicial, mas que a considera “equivocada”.

Segundo ele, em 2018 assumiu o governo de transição do então presidente eleito Jair Bolsonaro, e que começou uma interlocução com os governadores. Disse ainda que teve uma “parceria efetiva” em projetos do governador Ratinho Junior. Em 2022, disse que foi senador na mesma coligação do governador do Paraná.

Afirmou ainda que não é adversário de Ratinho Junior e que pretende manter alguns dos projetos do governador, mas não se aprofundou em quais seriam estes projetos.

Sergio Moro disse que, para a área da saúde, propõe a ‘Tabela SUS Paranaense’. Segundo ele, com o corte de gastos estadual que irá realizar no governo, vai complementar os pagamentos da tabela federal do SUS. A intenção, com isso, seria ampliar as ofertas de consultas, exames e cirurgias, para diminuir filas. O projeto, segundo Moro, é baseado em uma iniciativa implementada em São Paulo.

Ao ser questionado sobre a demanda do SUS na região de Foz do Iguaçu, que atende também estrangeiros vindos de regiões de fronteira, disse que terá um olhar para cada uma das regiões do Paraná e que apenas construir hospitais não resolve o problema. O candidato não detalhou o que fará especificamente na região Oeste, mas disse que a saúde será uma das prioridades do seu governo, caso eleito.

Aliança com o candidato Flávio Bolsonaro

Perguntado sobre o apoio a Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato à presidência pelo PL, que passou a ser investigado por corrupção e lavagem de dinheiro no caso do Banco Master, Sergio Moro disse que Flávio Bolsonaro “apresentou as explicações dele” e que "nunca obstruiu as investigações".

Moro disse que as investigações contra Flávio Bolsonaro vão seguir, que não tem “compromisso com o erro”, e que os questionamentos devem ser feitos para o candidato à presidência.

Sobre Waldemar da Costa Neto, presidente do PL, que foi condenado pelo STF por corrupção passiva e lavagem de dinheiro no Mensalão, Moro disse que o presidente do seu partido já cumpriu a pena e que "depois, não ouviu mais falar sobre envolvimento dele em coisas erradas". Disse ainda que não é Costa Neto quem vai governar o Paraná.

Sobre o serviço realizado pela Copel após a privatização, concluída em 2023, Moro afirmou que não é contrário à privatização e que pretende mantê-la. No entanto, disse que o objetivo da venda da empresa deveria ser mais eficiência e qualidade no serviço, mas que isso não aconteceu, segundo o candidato.

Ele afirmou que, se eleito governador, vai exigir da empresa um plano de investimentos e mudanças na direção que sejam necessárias. Disse que vai buscar a fiscalização da Copel junto às delegações federais e colocar a Procuradoria-Geral do Estado para “proteger” o cidadão paranaense em casos levados pelos consumidores à Justiça.

articles.title: Britânico confessa ter drogado e estuprado esposa por 21 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Os crimes ocorreram entre 2004 e 2025. Marido admitiu ter administrado uma substância à esposa com o objetivo de deixá-la inconsciente.
articles.summary: Os crimes ocorreram entre 2004 e 2025. Marido admitiu ter administrado uma substância à esposa com o objetivo de deixá-la inconsciente.
articles.body:
Um dos acusados de abusar de mulher chegando ao Tribunal em Manchester em 14 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: Temilade Adelaja/Reuters

Um homem britânico admitiu, nesta segunda-feira (14), ter drogado e estuprado repetidamente a própria esposa dentro de casa durante mais de duas décadas. A confissão foi feita pouco antes do início do julgamento.

O homem, que tem cerca de 60 anos e é do norte da Inglaterra , não pode ser identificado para preservar a identidade da esposa, que tem direito ao anonimato por toda a vida.

Ele se declarou culpado no Tribunal da Coroa de Minshull Street, em Manchester, de 45 acusações. Anteriormente, já havia admitido outros 15 crimes.

Entre as acusações estão 21 estupros, 15 agressões com penetração, 11 agressões sexuais e um crime de compartilhamento de imagens íntimas sem consentimento. Os crimes ocorreram entre 2004 e 2025.

Ele também admitiu ter administrado uma substância à esposa com o objetivo de deixá-la inconsciente.

Segundo os promotores, a mulher foi repetidamente estuprada e agredida sexualmente dentro da própria casa enquanto estava inconsciente, depois de ser drogada pelo marido.

Outros 12 homens, com idades entre 28 e 74 anos, também são acusados de abusar sexualmente da mulher entre 2018 e 2025. Todos negaram as acusações, que incluem estupro.

“Nosso foco continua sendo apoiar a vítima dessa terrível campanha de abuso ao longo dessa investigação muito complexa”, disse o subchefe da Polícia da Grande Manchester, Rick Jackson.

“Continua sendo prestado apoio especializado à vítima que está no centro deste caso.”

O julgamento dos outros homens será realizado no mesmo tribunal e deve durar vários meses.

O caso apresenta semelhanças com a história de Gisèle Pelicot , que chocou a França. Durante dez anos, Dominique Pelicot dopou a própria esposa e convidou desconhecidos para estuprá-la enquanto ela estava inconsciente.

A vítima não sabia dos abusos. O agressor foi condenado pela Justiça francesa no fim de 2024.

Segundo as investigações, os abusos contra Gisèle começaram em 2011. Ela foi estuprada pelo menos 92 vezes por 72 homens diferentes, com idades entre 21 e 68 anos.

Apesar disso, a acusação formal envolveu apenas 50 réus, além de Dominique Pelicot. Os outros 22 homens não foram encontrados ou identificados pelos investigadores.

Gisèle tinha o direito de permanecer anônima, mas decidiu mostrar o próprio rosto e pedir que o julgamento fosse aberto ao público. Segundo seus advogados, ela tomou a decisão para evitar que outras mulheres passassem por uma situação semelhante.

articles.title: FourC inaugura Bloco D e amplia estrutura educacional em Bauru | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação reuniu colaboradores, estudantes, famílias e autoridades e marcou o início das atividades dos alunos nos novos espaços da escola.
articles.summary: Programação reuniu colaboradores, estudantes, famílias e autoridades e marcou o início das atividades dos alunos nos novos espaços da escola.
articles.body:
Cerimônia de inauguração do novo Bloco D da FourC Bilingual Academy em Bauru — Foto: Bryan Assis

A FourC Bilingual Academy , uma escola brasileira bilíngue de Bauru (SP) que atende alunos da Educação Infantil ao Ensino Médio e High School, inaugurou nesta semana, um novo bloco que integra a expansão de sua estrutura na cidade. O Bloco D amplia os espaços destinados às atividades da escola e marca uma nova etapa na trajetória da instituição. A programação foi dividida em diversos momentos ao longo do segundo semestre. As comemorações reúnem colaboradores, alunos, famílias, comunidade, autoridades, pais pioneiros, que acompanham a FourC desde seus primeiros anos.

A primeira etapa ocorreu no dia 29 de agosto, com os colaboradores da FourC. E em 31 de agosto, alunos e famílias conheceram os novos ambientes e participaram simbolicamente da abertura das salas. A partir desse dia, os estudantes também passaram a utilizar o Bloco D em sua rotina, com o início das aulas nos novos espaços.

A programação seguiu do dia 2 de setembro, com uma cerimônia institucional que reuniu autoridades, convidados, famílias e pais pioneiros. Entre os presentes estavam a prefeita de Bauru, Suéllen Rosim , além de prefeitos da região, secretários municipais, diretoria regional de educação, entre outros.

“Ficamos felizes por, de certa forma, fazer parte dessa semente que a FourC está plantando. Ela irá gerar muitos frutos para Bauru e para o Brasil, porque muitas pessoas que sairão destas salas de aula irão conquistar o mundo graças ao trabalho de vocês”, destacou a prefeita.

Durante o encontro, os convidados puderam conhecer os novos ambientes em um tour pelo Bloco D . A programação, que marcou simbolicamente a concretização de um novo capítulo da história da FourC , terminou com um momento de confraternização entre os participantes.

O novo bloco amplia a estrutura da escola e foi pensado para receber alunos da Educação Infantil ao Primário I . Os ambientes fazem parte de uma proposta pedagógica que entende a estrutura escolar como um dos elementos da experiência educativa, criando possibilidades para convivência, investigação, criatividade e diferentes formas de aprender.

Além das salas de aula, o Bloco D conta com ginásio poliesportivo, teatro, sala de leituras e parque para as crianças . O teatro também deve ampliar a relação da escola com a cidade, com a previsão de receber, futuramente, peças e outros eventos artísticos abertos à comunidade.

Durante a cerimônia, a mantenedora Sara Hughes falou sobre a trajetória que tornou possível a expansão da escola e destacou o caráter coletivo desse percurso.

“Tudo o que existe aqui é, realmente, a construção de muitas mãos, muitas cabeças e muitos sonhos”, afirmou.

Ao projetar o futuro, Sara também ressaltou que o impacto do novo espaço estará relacionado às experiências vividas pelos estudantes e à forma como elas poderão se refletir na sociedade .

“O sucesso desse prédio será medido pelas contribuições que nossos alunos farão à sociedade. Nós queremos que eles sintam vontade, coragem e capacidade de construir futuros desejáveis para todos”, frisou.

Mantenedora Sara Hughes durante a cerimônia que marcou o início das atividades nos novos espaços — Foto: Bryan Assis

O compromisso com a comunidade também esteve presente no planejamento da expansão. O projeto foi desenvolvido considerando aspectos como mobilidade, segurança e convivência com o entorno. O Bloco D conta com 352 vagas para carros, motos e bicicletas , ampliando a estrutura de estacionamento da escola e contribuindo para organizar o fluxo de veículos na região da Vila Aviação.

A circulação entre os dois prédios da FourC será feita por uma passarela elevada sobre a Avenida Affonso José Aiello. A estrutura irá conectar o bloco atual ao Bloco D, oferecendo mais segurança nos deslocamentos.

O Bloco D integra a expansão da FourC , que, em seus 18 anos de trajetória em Bauru, tem como referências os pilares da cultura, colaboração, pensamento crítico e cidadania, representando os quatro C’s que dão nome à escola. A inauguração marca uma nova etapa de crescimento da instituição e amplia os espaços destinados às experiências educacionais dos estudantes . Mais do que ampliar fisicamente a escola, o Bloco D foi pensado para criar ambientes e experiências que estimulem esses valores no cotidiano dos alunos.

A nova estrutura também será apresentada à comunidade educacional da região durante o 6º Encontro FourC de Educadores , que acontece nos dias 25 e 26 de setembro , com o tema “Conexões que Importam” . Os participantes serão os primeiros educadores de Bauru e região a conhecerem e vivenciarem os novos espaços do Bloco D, incluindo o teatro da escola.

Com 12 horas de programação , o encontro reunirá profissionais de instituições públicas e privadas para atividades de formação, observação de aulas, workshops e troca de experiências, permitindo conhecer, na prática, como os novos ambientes se conectam à proposta pedagógica da FourC. Para mais informações e compra de ingresso, acesse:

Endereço: Av. Affonso José Aiello, 125, Bauru - SP

articles.title: Luciano Zucco propõe bloco de estados para renegociar dívida | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PL ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul participou nesta segunda-feira (14) de entrevista ao vivo.
articles.summary: Em entrevista à RBS TV, o candidato Luciano Zucco propõe articular SP, MG e RJ para renegociar a dívida do Rio Grande do Sul com a União.
articles.body:
O candidato do PL ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul, Luciano Zucco, afirmou nesta segunda-feira (14), em entrevista ao Jornal do Almoço, da RBS TV, que pretende articular uma negociação conjunta com São Paulo, Minas Gerais e Rio de Janeiro sobre as dívidas dos estados com a União.

Segundo Zucco, os quatro estados têm força econômica e política para buscar mudanças nas condições de pagamento. O candidato também afirmou que pretende usar a experiência como líder da oposição na Câmara dos Deputados nessa interlocução. A entrevista teve duração de 25 minutos.

"Nós não somos uma ilha e eu faço essa introdução justamente para dizer que é necessário uma interlocução muito efetiva, mostrando que o Rio Grande do Sul tem que ser respeitado ", afirmou.

O candidato ainda falou sobre como pretende reduzir o número de secretarias do atual governo, déficit fiscal, como retiraria moradores de áreas de risco em caso de nova enchente, políticas de irrigação e projetos de energia eólica.

Zucco também foi questionado sobre educação e saúde, quando comentou sobre modelo cívico-militar de ensino e como faria para diminuir a ambulancioterapia e as filas de atendimentos.

Luciano Lorenzini Zucco tem 52 anos, é natural de Alegrete e formado em Ciências Militares pela Academia Militar das Agulhas Negras. Por quase três décadas, atuou no Exército Brasileiro. Em 2018, estreou na política e foi eleito deputado estadual. Em 2022, foi eleito deputado federal para o atual mandato.

A entrevista abriu a série do Jornal do Almoço com os candidatos ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul nas eleições de 2026. Os candidatos de partidos, coligações e federações que possuem pelo menos cinco representantes no Congresso Nacional participam ao vivo. Os demais candidatos serão entrevistados em reportagens gravadas.

A ordem das entrevistas foi definida em sorteio na presença de representantes dos partidos. Veja o calendário:

14 de setembro: Luciano Zucco (PL), ao vivo;

15 de setembro: Gabriel Souza (MDB), ao vivo;

16 de setembro: Marcelo Maranata (PSDB), ao vivo;

17 de setembro: Juliana Brizola (PDT), ao vivo;

18 de setembro*: data reservada para entrevista ao vivo com candidato de partido sem cinco representantes no Congresso Nacional que alcance 5% das intenções de voto na pesquisa;

18 ou 19 de setembro*: entrevistas gravadas com Rejane de Oliveira (PSTU), Cesar Pontes (PCO) e Priscila Voigt (UP).

*Caso um candidato de partido sem cinco representantes no Congresso Nacional alcance 5% das intenções de voto na pesquisa, ele será entrevistado ao vivo na sexta-feira (18). Nessa situação, as entrevistas gravadas com os demais candidatos serão exibidas no sábado (19). Caso isso não ocorra, as entrevistas gravadas serão exibidas na sexta-feira (18). A ordem será definida por sorteio. Cada candidato terá 1 minuto e 30 segundos.

Dívida, déficit fiscal e redução de secretarias

Zucco afirmou que pretende reunir os governos do Rio Grande do Sul, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo e Minas Gerais para negociar as dívidas dos estados com a União. Segundo o candidato, a força política e econômica das quatro unidades da federação pode contribuir para o avanço das tratativas.

O candidato disse que já conversou com o governador de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas, sobre a proposta. Também afirmou que pretende usar a experiência de articulação no Congresso Nacional para tratar da dívida estadual.

"Eu já conversei com o Tarcísio, pela minha história, o Tarcísio é meu colega de turma de 34 anos, para mim um grande governador, falei para ele da importância dessa renegociação, ele vai entrar em campo comigo a partir de janeiro", afirmou.

Sobre a previsão de déficit de R$ 4,8 bilhões, resultado da diferença entre o que o estado gasta e arrecada, Zucco defendeu a redução do número de secretarias e de cargos de confiança como uma das medidas para reorganizar as contas públicas.

"Primeira coisa, nós vamos começar cortando de forma muito responsável o número de secretarias e cargos de confiança", afirmou.

Questionado sobre um plano alternativo caso a dívida não seja renegociada, Zucco defendeu uma agenda de desenvolvimento econômico para gerar renda e novos recursos.

Questionado sobre como agiria diante de um novo evento climático, Zucco defendeu a retirada de moradores das áreas de maior risco. O candidato citou a Ilha da Pintada, em Porto Alegre, como exemplo de local que precisa ser avaliado.

Segundo Zucco, profissionais qualificados devem classificar as áreas conforme os níveis de risco elevado, médio ou baixo. Ele também defendeu a participação das prefeituras, do Ministério Público e do Judiciário no processo.

"Acho que prioritariamente é tirar as pessoas da zona de risco", afirmou.

O candidato também propôs melhorar os sistemas de monitoramento e alarme e realizar obras que, segundo ele, poderiam ser executadas com maior rapidez. Questionado sobre quantas famílias pretende remover durante um eventual mandato, Zucco não apresentou estimativa. Ele disse que o número deve considerar o grau de risco e a disponibilidade de recursos.

"A gente tem que retirar o máximo possível. Se eu falar para ti que são mil, pode ser um número pequeno. Se eu falar que são 10 mil, passa do necessário", disse.

Zucco afirmou que pretende incentivar projetos de energia e ampliar a rede trifásica no interior do Rio Grande do Sul. Segundo o candidato, uma rede mais estável é necessária para apoiar uma política permanente de irrigação e contribuir para o desenvolvimento econômico.

O candidato também citou a energia eólica, a energia solar e a biomassa como potenciais do estado.

"A gente quer falar sobre uma política permanente de irrigação. Para isso, nós precisamos de uma energia mais estável, forte no interior, precisa avançar a energia trifásica", afirmou.

Zucco relacionou os investimentos em energia a uma agenda de geração de renda e novos recursos para o estado. O candidato também defendeu investimentos em infraestrutura logística, conectividade e internet no interior.

Zucco defendeu a ampliação do modelo cívico-militar nas escolas cujas comunidades tenham interesse na proposta. O candidato afirmou que o modelo não resolve sozinho os problemas da educação, mas pode contribuir para melhorar o ambiente escolar, a disciplina e o respeito aos professores — citou exemplos dos estados de São Paulo e Paraná.

Segundo Zucco, a implantação seria precedida de audiências públicas e de conversas com professores, pais, prefeituras e comunidades. O candidato afirmou que toda escola interessada teria de passar por esses procedimentos antes da adesão.

"Eu não vejo isso como solução, é uma alternativa. A gente vai levar para a comunidade ou para a prefeitura que assim entender", afirmou.

O candidato disse que o modelo proposto utilizaria militares da reserva como monitores fora da sala de aula. Segundo Zucco, as disciplinas e o trabalho dos professores permaneceriam os mesmos. Questionado sobre o custo da proposta, Zucco afirmou que o modelo cívico-militar indicado por ele é simples.

"O que é o custo talvez seja uniforme, mas o próprio monitor, ele por si só é um ou dois monitores para cada 90 alunos. Então, não é algo custoso e o resultado é muito positivo", disse.

Na saúde, Zucco defendeu o fortalecimento dos postos e o uso da telemedicina para ampliar o acesso dos moradores do interior a médicos especialistas. Segundo o candidato, um clínico-geral poderia consultar um especialista a distância durante o atendimento na unidade básica.

Zucco afirmou que a proposta reduziria os encaminhamentos e os gastos das prefeituras com o transporte de pacientes para a Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre.

"Já no posto de saúde, o clínico geral vai ter acesso a um especialista. Isso vai diminuir, inclusive, o encaminhamento, a ambulancioterapia", disse.

O candidato também defendeu que algumas especialidades sejam disponibilizadas presencialmente no interior. Questionado sobre a dificuldade para levar médicos especialistas ao interior, Zucco voltou a citar a telemedicina como alternativa.

"Há dificuldade, por isso que a gente quer trabalhar a questão da telemedicina e aquelas especialidades que são as mais necessitadas, oftalmologia e ortopedia, essas nós vamos buscar tentar levar para o interior", afirmou.

articles.title: JD Vance insists US is ‘on top of’ Houthi advance in Red Sea
articles.summary: US Vice President JD Vance says the Trump administration is “very much on top of” the Houthi advance in Yemen.

articles.title: Meet Noah Williams: The 9-year-old Melbourne programmer who learned C++ at 6, joined Mensa at 7 and became the world’s youngest computer programmer
articles.summary: Rest of World News: At an age when many children are just beginning to explore basic mathematics, Noah Williams was learning C++, one of the world’s most widely used prog.
articles.body: At an age when many children are just beginning to explore basic mathematics, Noah Williams was learning C++, one of the world’s most widely used programming languages. The Melbourne child began writing programmes to help with mathematical calculations at six, joined Mensa at seven after achieving an IQ score in the 99.9th percentile and later set a Guinness World Records title. On 8 August 2025, when he was eight years and 307 days old, an independent firm published one of Noah’s programmes, making him the youngest computer programmer recognised by Guinness World Records. As featured in Guinness World Records’ 2027 Young Achievers, Noah’s interests now extend beyond computer code to robotics and drones, offering a glimpse of how quickly a child’s curiosity can grow into professional-level technical work.Love of numbersNoah’s first exposure to programming was through math. Programming was not a new subject to him, but a means to do calculations and search for patterns. Programming enabled him to tell a computer what to do and then observe what happened. C++ is not usually thought of as a language for beginners. It is a powerful and general-purpose language used in software, games, engineering, finance, and scientific applications. It demands careful attention because minor mistakes in syntax or logic can cause a program to malfunction. At six, Noah began learning the language and creating programmes to assist with mathematical calculations. The achievement was not simply that he could type code. To write a functioning programme, he had to understand sequences, conditions, variables and the relationship between an instruction and its outcome. Kids tend to learn in bursts of curiosity . They become deeply interested in things that fascinate them .In Noah’s case, mathematics and programming provided a framework for investigating questions and building solutions.Joining Mensa at sevenBy the age of seven, Noah had joined Mensa, an international high IQ society. Guinness World Records reported that he achieved an IQ score in the 99.9th percentile. An intelligence test result does not explain everything about a child’s abilities or future. Programming also requires patience, creativity, persistence and the willingness to revise an idea when it does not work. Noah’s story includes those practical qualities as much as the numerical achievement. Learning C++ at a young age suggests that he was able to engage with abstract concepts earlier than many children. But ability alone does not create a working programme. He would also have needed opportunities to practise, access to suitable technology and support from adults who recognised and encouraged his interests. Mensa membership became one milestone in his development, but it was the continued application of his skills that eventually led to the Guinness record.How he set the recordGuinness World Records defines the record as the youngest person to programme computers. Its criteria describe a programmer as someone who develops and writes computer programmes, while a programme is a set of instructions written in a language that a computer can understand and execute. Noah met that standard when one of his programmes was published by an independent firm. The publication date was 8 August 2025, when Noah was eight years and 307 days old. Guinness lists the record location as Melbourne, Australia, and records the achievement under the title “youngest professional computer programmer.”The distinction between learning to code and having a programme published is important. Many children experiment with programming through educational platforms, games and simple projects. Noah’s record required evidence that his work had reached a professional level and had been published independently. The achievement does not mean he was the first child ever to write code. It means Guinness verified him under a specific record category based on his age and the publication of his programme.From calculations to roboticsNoah’s interests have expanded beyond traditional computer programming. Guinness World Records’ Young Achievers profile says he has also worked with robots and drones. These fields build on the same principles as software development but apply them to physical systems. A robot may use code to respond to sensors, move its parts or complete a task. A drone can rely on programming for navigation, stabilisation, image capture and automated flight. Working with hardware introduces new challenges. Code has to work with motors, cameras, batteries and sensors, but the physical world is unpredictable. A program running in a simulation may behave differently when a robot crashes into an obstacle, or a drone runs into wind. For Noah, moving from screen-based programming to machines is a natural extension of his curiosity. He can write instructions, see how a device responds and change the design. It’s a direct and visible mix of math, engineering and programming.What makes young programmers differentA child who starts programming early may develop a different relationship with technology. Instead of seeing computers as just devices for entertainment or communication, the child may view them as tools to build systems and solve problems. That perspective can encourage experimentation. A young programmer may ask how a game works, how a drone knows where to fly or how a computer can complete a calculation. Each question can lead to another project. However, it is important not to turn exceptional children into unrealistic symbols. Young programmers still need time to play, rest and develop socially. Their interests should be encouraged, but not by turning every activity into a competition or by demanding constant achievement. Noah’s record is a recognition of a specific accomplishment, not a measure of his entire identity. The most valuable aspect of his story may be the opportunity to keep exploring rather than the title itself.The role of supportTechnical talent develops within an environment. Noah likely benefited from access to computers, teaching resources and adults willing to answer questions or find appropriate challenges. Children can be very curious, but without encouragement and practical opportunities, that curiosity may go unexplored. Families and schools can help young programmers by providing structured opportunities for learning but still leaving room for independent discovery. Beginner tools can introduce programming concepts, and more advanced languages like C++ can be introduced when the child is ready for greater complexity. Mentors can also help young students understand that failure is normal. A programme that does not run is not necessarily a bad idea. Debugging teaches patience, logic and the ability to identify mistakes without giving up. The same support can help children from less advantaged backgrounds. Access to computers, broadband, clubs and coding education is uneven, and talent exists in every community. Expanding opportunities is essential if more young people are to discover their abilities.Recognition in Guinness World Records 2027Noah is featured among the Young Achievers in Guinness World Records 2027, a group of under-16-year-olds recognised for unusual accomplishments. Guinness describes the group as young people who have shown that age is not an obstacle to achievement. Being included alongside other young record holders places Noah’s technical work in a broader context. The group includes children and teenagers who have pursued achievements in different fields, demonstrating that young people can make meaningful contributions in science, sport, performance and creative work. The recognition also introduces his story to audiences who may not normally follow computer programming. A record title can make a technical achievement easier to understand and may encourage other children to try coding. Noah's challenge will be to keep developing his interests without being defined only by the record. Technology changes quickly, and the skills that matter most will include creativity, collaboration and the ability to learn new systems.A beginning rather than an endingNoah Williams became the world’s youngest computer programmer after learning C++ at six, joining Mensa at seven and having one of his programmes published at eight. His record captures an unusual moment in a young life, but it does not predict exactly what he will do next. He may continue with software, robotics or drones, or move into fields that do not yet exist in their current form. The important foundation is his ability to ask questions and turn ideas into working systems. For other children, his story offers encouragement without requiring imitation. Not every child needs to learn C++ at six, or go for a world record. The bigger lesson is that curiosity can become powerful when given time, guidance and freedom to develop. By age nine, Noah already shows what can happen when a child sees computers not simply as machines to be used, but as tools for thinking, creating and discovering.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Disha Salian death case: CBI registers FIR, takes over probe from Mumbai Police
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, former manager of late acto.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, days after the Bombay high court ordered a central agency probe into the case.The FIR follows the high court's September 2 order directing the CBI to register a case and conduct a fresh investigation into Salian's death. The court had criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR despite the investigation continuing for nearly six years, observing that it "raises more questions than answers".The bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and Ranjitsinha Raja Bhonsale had said a case investigation could not continue for an inordinately long period and directed the CBI to appoint a suitably experienced and senior officer to investigate the matter.The court also directed the Mumbai Police to hand over all case papers to the CBI and record the statement of Salian's father, Satish Salian. It made clear that registration of the FIR did not mean that anyone would automatically be treated as an accused."Nobody shall be treated as an accused unless, in the opinion of the investigating officer, there are sufficient grounds to raise reasonable suspicion against him depending on the material collected during the investigation," the court said.Salian, 28, died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in Mumbai's Malad area. Mumbai Police had registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) and, following an inquiry, concluded that her death was a suicide.The high court pointed to what it described as "glaring discrepancies" in the police investigation, including the timing of the spot panchnama and questions concerning injuries sustained by Salian.Salian's father had approached the high court alleging that his daughter was raped and murdered and seeking a CBI investigation. He had also sought an FIR against Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, though the high court refrained from making findings against any individual.Salian had briefly worked as Rajput's manager. Rajput was found dead at his Mumbai residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian's death. A separate CBI probe into Rajput's death was ordered, with the agency later filing a closure report stating that he died by suicide.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: After Crocodile Hunter Steve Irwin died in 2006, Australia protected 330,000 Cape York acres in his name; the reserve now shelters over 40 significant species
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover the Steve Irwin Wildlife Reserve, a 330,000-acre conservation area created in memory of Steve Irwin, protecting over 40 significant species and diverse ecosystems on Cape York Peninsula.
articles.body: Steve Irwin died in 2006, after which a 330,000-acre property on Australia's Cape York Peninsula became part of a conservation effort bearing his name. The Steve Irwin Wildlife Reserve was established as a tribute to his conservation work and is now a protected landscape that contains rainforests, wetlands, savannas and dozens of species considered important for conservation.Australia Zoo says that the property was formerly known as Bertiehaugh Station, a cattle property on the western side of Cape York. The Australian Government purchased the property after Irwin’s death as a living memorial to his conservation work, while the Irwin family and Australia Zoo took on its management under Australia's National Reserves System. The reserve covers about 135,000 hectares, or 330,000 acres, and its southern end fronts the Wenlock River, while the Ducie River forms a northern boundary.The property soon faced a mining threatAustralia Zoo says that plans were announced to mine the area for bauxite, only days after the property was named the Steve Irwin Wildlife Reserve. The proposed development threatened to clear vegetation and remove bauxite from beneath the topsoil. The Irwin family responded with a campaign to protect the reserve, while supporters also petitioned the Queensland government.Queensland Parliament records from 2010 describe the 330,000-acre property as a wetland conservation area and tribute to Irwin. The parliamentary petition said a proposed mining area of about 30,300 acres included parts of the reserve and contained headwaters and spring-fed wetlands that were important to the Wenlock River and surrounding habitat.Australia Zoo says that the campaign involved millions of dollars and lasted six years before the Australian Government passed legislation protecting the reserve from the proposed strip mining. The reserve was subsequently given additional protection as a Strategic Environmental Area.More than 40 species have conservation significanceThe reserve contains 35 different ecosystems and currently has more than 40 species considered to have conservation significance because they are threatened, endemic or have restricted distributions. Its biodiversity records include 170 bird species, 48 fish species, 47 reptiles, 21 amphibians and 20 mammals. Australia Zoo says wildlife surveys are still being conducted, which means that the inventory can change as researchers continue working in the area.Australia Zoo says more than 48 freshwater fish species have been recorded in the Wenlock River, and the reserve contains one of the world's larger breeding populations of saltwater crocodiles. The property also contains unusual habitats that are associated with perched bauxite springs. Australia Zoo describes one spring forest ecosystem as unique, with no comparable ecosystem currently known elsewhere.The reserve remains a research siteAustralia Zoo and the University of Queensland have supported research programs on the reserve covering biodiversity, hydrology, fire ecology, palaeontology and archaeology. Scientists have also studied species including estuarine crocodiles, palm cockatoos, microbats, spiders, file snakes, carnivorous plants and northern quolls.Australia Zoo says that more than 170 crocodiles are currently being tracked in the Wenlock River, with the Irwin family continuing annual research trips to the reserve, and the scale of the property helps explain why the mining proposal generated such a prolonged conservation campaign. A development footprint of roughly 30,300 acres would have occupied only part of a 330,000-acre reserve, but the proposed area included important waterways and wetlands.Today, the Steve Irwin Wildlife Reserve remains a 330,000-acre conservation property on Cape York, with ongoing ecological research and surveys across its 35 ecosystems. Australia Zoo says the area currently supports more than 40 species of conservation significance.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 1869, 100 sheep were introduced to Mexico's Socorro Island; the herd grew to about 5,000 and damaged 30% of the island, then removing 1,762 helped forest cover rise from 29% to 85%
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Imagine an island where a herd introduced for ranching gradually became one of the biggest threats to its native ecosystem. That is what happened on M.
articles.body: Imagine an island where a herd introduced for ranching gradually became one of the biggest threats to its native ecosystem. That is what happened on Mexico’s Socorro Island, where about 100 sheep introduced in 1869 eventually became feral and reached an estimated 5,000 animals by 1960. Over decades, overgrazing contributed to severe vegetation loss and erosion across the island. A 2016 study published in Forests, titled “Recovery of Vegetation Cover and Soil after the Removal of Sheep in Socorro Island, Mexico”, documented how the landscape began recovering after the animals were removed. A separate 2019 study on the island’s ecological restoration recorded the eradication of 1,762 feral sheep between 2009 and 2012.How 100 sheep became an ecological problemSocorro Island is part of Mexico’s Revillagigedo Archipelago in the Pacific Ocean. Covering about 132 square kilometres, it is a volcanic island with a high level of biological endemism. The 2016 study notes that around 27% of its 117 vascular plant species are endemic, meaning they are found nowhere else. The island also has native terrestrial fauna that evolved in isolation from large herbivorous mammals.The sheep were introduced in 1869 for ranching. With no natural predators capable of controlling their numbers, they became feral and adapted to the island. Their population was estimated at around 5,000 by 1960. Hunting by the Mexican Navy later reduced the population to about 2,000 by 1988, but sheep remained a major source of ecological disturbance. The problem was not simply the number of animals. Their repeated grazing removed vegetation, damaged seedlings and disturbed the litter layer covering the soil. Sheep trails and resting areas also contributed to soil compaction. Once vegetation disappeared, the exposed soil became more vulnerable to erosion, particularly during heavy rainfall and tropical storms.According to the 2016 study, sheep were associated with the loss of soil and vegetation cover across about 30% of the island’s surface. More than 2,000 hectares of native vegetation had been lost over the period of degradation.Why the island was especially vulnerableSocorro’s geography made the consequences of vegetation loss more serious. The island lies in the path of tropical cyclones, meaning heavy rainfall could turn already exposed and compacted ground into channels of runoff and erosion. The researchers explained that reduced plant cover increased runoff, while sheep trails provided pathways through which water could move. This contributed to the formation of deep erosion gullies in some areas. Over time, the combination of grazing, soil disturbance and storms altered habitats that had previously supported native vegetation.The sheep also affected the composition of the plant community. Their grazing reduced native vegetation while helping some introduced plant species spread. The resulting landscape therefore was not simply a forest with fewer trees; it was an ecosystem whose vegetation structure and species composition had changed.The ecological consequences extended beyond plants and soil. According to the 2019 study, feral sheep destroyed roughly one-third of the island’s habitat, while feral cats created another major threat to native wildlife. Together, the two invasive mammals contributed to the disappearance of the Socorro dove and Socorro elf owl from the wild.The long campaign to remove the sheepEfforts to eliminate the feral sheep intensified in the late 2000s. The eradication programme ran from 2009 to 2012 and combined aerial and ground-based methods. During the aerial phase, hunters removed 1,257 sheep. The campaign then shifted to ground hunting and trapping, with another 505 animals dispatched. The final stages also involved specially selected “Judas sheep”, which were fitted with radio-telemetry collars and released to help locate remaining animals. Hunting dogs were subsequently used to track the last few sheep. In total, 1,762 sheep were removed during the three-year eradication campaign.The goal was not merely to reduce the population but to eliminate the feral sheep from the island. Once grazing pressure disappeared, researchers could observe whether the damaged ecosystem was capable of recovering naturally.Vegetation returned surprisingly quicklyThe results provided a striking indication of the island’s ecological resilience. Researchers compared vegetation using satellite imagery from 2008 and 2013 and also conducted field assessments across 20 transects. The satellite analysis identified about 1,452 hectares where vegetation cover had increased between the two periods, equivalent to roughly 11% of the island’s surface. The field measurements were even more striking in some habitats. In forest sites examined by the researchers, average vegetation cover increased from 29.29% in 2009 to 85% in 2013. Mixed scrub areas rose from 19.17% to 72.5%, while eroded surfaces increased from 14.29% to 50.29%. The number of plant species recorded also increased across the studied habitats.The recovery was not limited to the amount of vegetation. Soil conditions also began to improve. Researchers found that areas with recovering vegetation showed improvements in several soil properties. Nitrogen and organic carbon levels were roughly twice those measured in eroded sites, while phosphorus and calcium values were substantially higher. Soil compaction also showed signs of recovery as vegetation returned.What the sheep removal revealedThe Socorro Island case demonstrates how quickly an invasive herbivore can alter an isolated ecosystem, but it also shows the potential for natural recovery once the pressure is removed. The researchers described the vegetation recovery as passive, meaning large-scale replanting was not required for the initial rebound. Native, endemic and some introduced plants began colonising areas that had previously been heavily degraded. However, the recovery did not mean that every ecological problem disappeared. The 2016 research found that some exotic plant species also became part of the recovering vegetation. Meanwhile, feral cats remained a serious conservation challenge. A later restoration report recorded continued efforts to eradicate them, with 502 cats removed by December 2016.Socorro Island therefore offers a more complicated lesson than simply “remove the invasive species and nature returns”. The removal of sheep removed one of the strongest pressures on the landscape, allowing vegetation and soil conditions to improve. But protecting an isolated ecosystem also requires dealing with other invasive species and ensuring that recovering native habitats remain viable.More than a century after the introduction of those first 100 sheep, the island’s experience shows how a seemingly small human intervention can have consequences lasting generations. It also demonstrates the remarkable capacity of an ecosystem to begin repairing itself once a major source of disturbance is finally removed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Water bottle sold above MRP at temple: Commission orders Rs 7 lakh penalty
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: The Kakinada district consumer commission has ordered a temple shop licensee to pay Rs 7 lakh to the consumer welfare fund for charging Rs .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Kakinada district consumer commission has ordered a temple shop licensee to pay Rs 7 lakh to the consumer welfare fund for charging Rs 25 for a one-litre water bottle marked at Rs 18. The commission also ordered a refund of Rs 7, Rs 10,000 compensation and Rs 5,000 litigation costs to the consumer. The order was passed on August 28, 2026.Why did the consumer approach the commission?According to the commission order, D Venkateswara Rao visited Sri Veera Venkata Satyanarayana Swamy Temple at Annavaram on February 22, 2026. He bought a one-litre packaged drinking water bottle from a shop run by the temple's licensee.The bottle had an MRP of Rs 18, but the shop charged him Rs 25 through UPI. When Rao questioned the price, the shopkeeper allegedly said he was authorised to sell the bottle above its MRP. Rao also complained to the temple administration through WhatsApp but said there was no action from their side.The shopkeeper denied the claim of charging Rs 25 for only the water bottle, he said the complainant had also bought a Rs 20 cool drink and a Rs 5 biscuit packet, and that the Rs 25 payment was for those items.The temple administration also denied responsibility. It said the shop was run by an independent licensee and that it had taken action against the licensee after receiving complaints about overcharging.What did the commission find?The bench comprising President Ch. Raghupathy Vasantha Kumar and member Chakka Susi and member Chaganti Nageswara Rao said the UPI payment proof, photograph of the water bottle and other evidence supported Rao's claim. It also noted that the licensee had not produced convincing documents to support his version that the Rs 25 payment was for a cool drink and biscuit.The commission found that Rao had bought only the water bottle and that the licensee had charged Rs 25 against the printed MRP of Rs 18. It further noted that the temple administration had received earlier complaints about overcharging by the same licensee and had issued several notices against him.The commission said the MRP printed on a packaged product is the highest price at which it can legally be sold to a consumer. Charging more than the printed MRP is not allowed."Such conduct squarely falls within the definition of "unfair trade practice" under Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, as it adopts an unfair method for promoting and supplying goods by violating statutory law and misleading consumers regarding the lawful sale price. It also amounts to deficiency in service, since the consumer is deprived of the protection guaranteed by law," the commission said.The commission said the matter was more serious because the sale took place at a major pilgrimage centre, where thousands of devotees visit every day. It said people buying essential items such as drinking water at such places may have little choice but to pay the price demanded."Consumers purchasing essential commodities such as drinking water at such places are ordinarily left with little or no bargaining power and are compelled to purchase at the price demanded. Exploiting such circumstances to collect amounts above the statutory MRP is a serious unfair trade practice affecting not merely one consumer, but the consumer public at large," it observed.The commission said the temple administration had supervisory control over the licensed shops but found no evidence that it had instructed or allowed the licensee to charge more than the MRP.It therefore dismissed the complaint against the temple administration and did not order it to pay any money. However, it directed the temple authorities to make sure that all licensed shops clearly display the MRP of packaged products.The temple administration was also directed to make announcements at hourly intervals asking devotees to buy goods at MRP and not pay more. It was also told to maintain an effective complaint system for devotees.The commission said simply returning the extra Rs 7 would not be enough because similar overcharging could affect many other consumers."If the Commission were to merely direct refund of the excess amount collected from the complainant, the opposite party would still stand to benefit from similar illegal collections made from innumerable other consumers. Such an approach would render the statutory prohibition ineffective and would encourage repetition of the violation. The Consumer Protection Act is a beneficial legislation enacted not merely to compensate an individual consumer but also to ensure fairness in trade, protect the consumer community at large, and eliminate unfair trade practices from the marketplace," it said.The commission therefore ordered the licensee to pay Rs 7 lakh as punitive damages to the Consumer Welfare Fund. It said the amount was meant to discourage such practices and protect consumers at public places and pilgrimage centres.The licensee was also ordered to refund Rs 7 to Rao, pay him Rs 10,000 compensation and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs. The directions have to be followed within 45 days, failing which the monetary amounts will carry 9 percent annual interest from the date of default until payment.
